headword: {平家物語|へいけものがたり}
gloss: The Tale of the Heike (medieval war chronicle)

definitions.explanation: A war tale of the Kamakura period describing the rise and fall of the Taira ({平家|へいけ}) clan in the Genpei War (1180–1185). Spread by blind monks who chanted it to the biwa lute, it is the great work on the Buddhist theme that all glory passes.

examples.japanese: {平家物語|へいけものがたり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{軍記物語|ぐんきものがたり}だ。
examples.english: The Tale of the Heike is a war tale.

examples.japanese: {平家物語|へいけものがたり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{冒頭|ぼうとう}→冒頭：11725_boutou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}えています→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you remember the opening of The Tale of the Heike?

examples.japanese: {琵琶法師|びわほうし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{平家物語|へいけものがたり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{語|かた}り→語り：14390_katari⟧ながら⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧した。
examples.english: Biwa-playing monks traveled from place to place reciting The Tale of the Heike.

notes:
Its opening lines are among the best-known passages in Japanese literature; schoolchildren recite them, and phrases from them are used in everyday comment on the fall of the powerful.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧、⟦{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}→諸行無常：14481_shogyoumujou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{響|ひび}き→響き：00098_hibiki⟧あり: "The bell of the Gion monastery echoes the impermanence of all things" — the opening line
- {驕|おご}れる⟦{者|もの}→者：12734_mono⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{久|ひさ}しからず: "the proud do not last long" — quoted when the arrogant fall
- ⟦{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}→盛者必衰：15558_joushahissui⟧: whoever flourishes must decline

CULTURAL NOTE:
Its episodes — the young {敦盛|あつもり} killed at {一ノ谷|いちのたに}, the archer {那須与一|なすのよいち} hitting a fan on a boat, the drowning of the child emperor at {壇ノ浦|だんのうら} — became the source for countless noh plays, kabuki, and modern dramas.
